title: The Disappearing Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift
one_line: In S&P futures the pre-FOMC drift was 0.49% per meeting in 1994-2011, still 0.45% for press-conference meetings to 2015, but only 0.09% (insignificant) in 2016-2019 and ≈0 without press conferences; the decline lines up with lower VIX.

findings.statement: Mean pre-FOMC return (prior open → 15 min before announcement): 0.492% (1994-2011, 131 meetings).
Press-conference meetings: 0.445% (Apr 2011-Dec 2015) → 0.092% (2016-2019, not significant); no-press-conference meetings −0.051%.
Adding VIX makes the post-liftoff dummy insignificant; VIX coefficient ≈ 0.23 (t ≈ 3.3).
Authors reject publication-driven decay as the main cause.

why.pattern: Uncertainty premium: the drift pays for resolving high policy uncertainty and fades when uncertainty is low.
why.mechanism: Pre-FOMC returns scale with VIX/TYVIX two days before the meeting.

tradable_edge: Trade the pre-FOMC long only when pre-meeting uncertainty is high (VIX or our AvgRange proxy above its 1-year median).

decay_risk.reason: Documents the decay; small samples (20 meetings per sub-period).

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
caveats: Read by Claude in a chat session (manual run 2), not by the weekly pipeline.
